title: Introducing Clef-omni with full multimodality, plus a faster Clef and a cheaper Clef-flash
key_facts: Cloudflare released Clef-omni, a decision model taking audio, video, image and text input, with weights open on Hugging Face.
It follows last week's release of Clef and Clef-flash, Cloudflare's open-weight decision models.
Clef-omni is built on Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct and scores options without generating text.
Cloudflare says text decisions return in about 130 ms at the median, images about 150 ms, and a 21-second video clip with sound in about 1.5 seconds.
Clef-flash is now cheaper than TypeSafe's Jev, but its hosted context window drops from 64k to 24k tokens; weights still support 256k for self-hosting.
Cloudflare says only 0.24% of requests exceeded 24k input tokens.
The hosted Clef is faster after moving to SGLang; no new weights were released for that.
Cloudflare teams use Clef to close spam issues, moderate plugins for phishing, scan for personal data and detect malicious domains.
quote_evidence: Today, we're releasing Clef-omni, which takes in audio and video input alongside text and image.
We also cut the price of Clef-flash so it is now cheaper than Jev, and we made Clef faster.
The hosted version of Clef-flash now has a context window of 24k, instead of 64k as previously advertised.
why_it_matters_hint: One cheap model can now make choices over mixed media, replacing chains of separate models.
event_date: 9 Oct 2026; Clef first released the week before
notes: Company blog post; all speed and price claims are Cloudflare's own. Follow-up of the 9 Oct 2026 pool item (InfoQ: Cloudflare open sources decision models).
